why: Look at the black dot first. It sits on a corner of the hexagon and moves one corner anticlockwise in every figure: right, top-right, top-left, left. So the next dot must be at the bottom-left corner. Only options 1 and 5 have a dot there. The arrow keeps turning clockwise (right, down-right, down-left, left), so the next arrow points up-left. Option 1 has an arrow pointing down-right, which would be a big backward jump, so option 5 is correct.
trick: When a figure has two moving parts, track each part separately, then cross out options that break either rule. The dot rule alone cuts the options to two.
note: Dot rule is clear (one hexagon corner anticlockwise each step), leaving options 1 and 5. Arrow turns clockwise by uneven steps (45, 90, 45), so its next step is not fully certain; option 5 (up-left, +45) fits best, option 2 (up, +90) has no dot.
